hints.title: Dislike Edge 2-Coloring Obstacle
hints.text: Partitioning n people into two distinct groups such that no mutually disliked pair shares the same group requires modeling dislikes as edges. How can alternating groups across dislike connections expose conflicts?

hints.title: Mutual Dislike Parity Invariant
hints.text: Build an undirected graph where each dislike relationship is an edge. The graph is partitionable if and only if every connected component is bipartite.

hints.title: Component Bicolor Alternation Procedure
hints.text: Build an adjacency list for n people. Maintain color array of size n + 1 with 0. For each person i from 1 to n: if uncolored, set color[i] = 1 and enqueue i. For each dislike neighbor v: if color[v] == color[u], return false. If uncolored, set color[v] = -color[u] and enqueue. If all finish, return true.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Graph construction takes O(E) and two-color check takes O(N + E).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing 2^N partition combinations is exponentially impossible.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency list and color tracking consume linear space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that dislike constraints map directly to bipartite graph 2-colorability.
